title: Bonus: Original Turtle Trading Rules

claims.text: A complete trading specification covers universe, size, entry, loss exits, profitable exits and execution tactics.
claims.anchor: Tactics: How to buy or sell

claims.text: Volatility sizing requires true range, its initialization and smoothing, contract multipliers and whole-contract truncation; equal estimated volatility does not equal identical loss distributions.
Portfolio limits include instrument, correlated-group and directional exposure; they reduce exposure but cannot enforce a maximum loss during gaps.
The appendix specifies 20-day and 55-day breakout systems using preceding days and intraday triggers, distinct from close-to-next-open demonstration systems.
The shorter system's prior-breakout filter tracks skipped hypothetical trades as well as executed trades and includes a longer-breakout fallback; state must be maintained causally.
Pyramiding uses actual fills and explicit stop updates; ambiguous printed fractions must be reconciled before any implementation.
Reject literal assurances that preset stop distances cap realized trade or portfolio loss; gaps, nonfills and repeated entries can exceed those budgets.
claims.anchor: total risk would never exceed 2 percent

claims.text: Exit rules interact with entries and sizing; the appendix specifies 10-day exits for System 1 and 20-day exits for System 2.
Limit orders trade price control for execution uncertainty; fast-market delays require explicit handling and cannot be assumed to improve every fill.
Simultaneous signal selection, contract-month choice and rollover are strategy decisions that require deterministic definitions and liquidity checks.
Inspect the actual trade and equity history and independently test a fully specified policy before relying on someone else's summarized results.
claims.anchor: look at the daily equity logs

assimilation: Treat the appendix as a historical family of related rules, not a turnkey approved strategy. Preserve causal windows, fill-dependent state, portfolio limits, skipped-signal state and roll handling, and reject hard-loss guarantees. Require reconciliation and independent evaluation before adoption.
adversarial_review: The appendix calls the system wholly mechanical but grants discretion over markets, strategy allocation, strength measures, annual sizing and fast-market timing. Its 55-day long breakout differs from earlier 60-day and 10-week descriptions. N's displayed recurrence uses weight 1/20, not the common EMA span-20 weight 2/21. Page 212's November 6 true range prints .0130 although previous close .6923 and low .6800 imply .0123. Page 213 uses December 4 N for December 6 without explaining the intervening day. Pages 218 and 221 visibly print 1-and-a-half N where surrounding prose and worked tables imply half N; preserve the conflict. Page 223 visibly prints half N stops with one-and-a-half percent risk, inconsistent with 1% per N and its half-N table. Account reductions say each 10% of original equity but the example compounds the reduced base, and starting February 1983 conflicts with the earlier 1984 chronology. The 2% trade-risk language does not mean a four-unit position has at most 2% cumulative entry loss; the standard example has unequal distances to a common stop. Moving-average exits are implicit exit rules, not guaranteed bounded losses. Waiting for stabilization conflicts with immediate stop execution and may worsen losses. Bid/ask liquidity is not present at all times and displayed prices can disappear. Claims about strongest contracts almost always outperforming and failure being solely noncompliance are unproven. Independent testing must include costs, slippage, delivery deadlines and all attempted variants. Bibliography 232-234 discloses author-linked commercial resources; inspected index 235-257 and blank/end matter 258-259 add navigation, not independent evidence or additional books read.
memory_delta: Specify and independently test one unambiguous variant before use. Historical Turtle rules include state, discretion and inconsistent printed numbers. Volatility targets and stops do not cap realized loss; causal timing, actual fills, constraints and roll mechanics are essential.
reading_provenance: Read all PDF pages 205-231, inspected all displayed formulas and worked sizing/stop tables. Separately inspected bibliography/index/end matter 232-259; no linked books or sites counted as read.
